Approval fatigue.d: When people see so many routine approval prompts that they start approving without reading, so the important prompt gets waved through too.

Audit log.d: A permanent, time-stamped record of who or what did each action, with what permissions and who approved it, used to reconstruct what happened.

Trajectory evaluation.d: Judging an agent by the path it took (tools called, order, approvals, forbidden actions, steps) as well as by its final result.

Shadow mode.d: A rollout stage where an agent runs on real inputs but only records what it would have done, so people can compare without real consequences.

Canary release.d: Releasing a change, or more autonomy for an agent, to a small group first and watching closely before rolling it out to everyone.

Kill switch.d: A control outside the AI that stops an agent or a capability immediately, works without the agent's cooperation and fails closed.

Software development lifecycle.d: The stages every change passes through from idea to running software: plan, design, code, review, test, release and operate. Often shortened to SDLC.

DORA metrics.d: Software delivery measures from the DORA research programme: change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time, change fail rate and deployment rework rate.

Minimal reproduction.d: The smallest set of steps, data or code that still makes a bug happen, which makes it far easier to investigate.

Correlation ID.d: An identifier attached to one request and written into every log line in every service it passes through, so you can follow that request end to end.

Git bisect.d: A git command that finds the commit that introduced a bug by repeatedly testing the commit halfway between a known good and a known bad one.

Root-cause analysis.d: Investigating why a problem really happened, beyond the visible symptom, so that fixes prevent the whole class of problem. Often shortened to RCA.

Five whys.d: A root-cause technique of repeatedly asking why something happened until you reach a cause in the process that can be changed.

Blameless postmortem.d: An incident write-up that focuses on what in the system allowed a failure, not on who to blame, so people share details honestly.
